text:
incident-bot: P0 alert: sustained spike in external extension runtime calls (extension_api) causing CPU saturation on fleet pool A. Auto-mitigation kicked: soft-rate-limit applied to extension_api. Investigating now.

sam: saw it, paging in. dropping into channel. what's the impact surface? any customer 5xx? :eyes:

maria: metrics -> error rate up, tail latency up for tokens > 1k. Most traffic from actionhook integration (third-party connectors). Top 3 tenants account for ~60% of offending traffic.

will: confirm we have auto-limit rule but need stricter shaping. proposing: reduce per-tenant qps and disable rich object outputs for non-enterprise tiers to cut exec surface.

sam: agree. can we flip flag for free+pro quickly? how do we do it safely?

maria: two steps: 1) apply ratecap patch on edge routing for extension_api; 2) set feature flag to force plain-text outputs (disable "rich object outputs") for affected plans. I'll apply 1. @will can you push 2?

will: on it. patching rate limits now.
```bash
# apply edge rate limit, scope: extension_api, tiers: free, pro
curl -sS -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/ops/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"extension_api","scope_filter":"plan:free,plan:pro","qps":2,"burst":5,"reason":"emergency runtime protection"}'
```

ops-bot: Rate limit rule created: rule_id=rl-20260301-73; scope=extension_api; qps=2; burst=5; applied to edge clusters in us-west/us-east within 90s.

will: applying feature flag now to force plain-text responses for non-enterprise. pushing to console feature-flags service.
```json
{ "flag": "force_plain_extension_output", "value": "on", "targets": ["plan:free","plan:pro"], "note": "emergency - reduce exec surface" }
```

ops-bot: Feature flag updated: force_plain_extension_output=on for plan:free,plan:pro. rollout_percent=100.

maria: monitoring: CPU and tail latency trending down after ratecap + flag. error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% in 5m window. Good signal.

sam: any known customer-facing errors? Kyla from CX looped in? @kyla?

kyla: received two tickets from integrations customers experiencing degraded features (rich outputs missing). CS drafting comms: short note explaining temporary restriction to stabilize service; will include ETA 2 hours and contact if urgent.

jess: preparing handoff in 30m. summary for next on-call: rate limits rl-20260301-73 applied, feature flag force_plain_extension_output enabled for free/pro, tiered premium unaffected. Monitor latency, error rates, and key tenant logs (tenant IDs: t-178, t-402, t-990).

sam: good. add action items: 1) SRE to validate rollback safe path if backend stabilizes 2) Platform to prepare targeted throttle if rl impacts false positives 3) CS to notify top 5 tenants and offer assist.

will: I'll keep a watch on extension_api KPIs for next hour, will post updates. If error rate stays <5% keep this config; if <2% for 20m we can cautiously relax qps to 5.

maria: logging note: collected sample traces for top offending calls and uploaded to /artifacts/incident/1744029999. saved one larger sample for infra team.

sam: thanks all. tagging page to incident log and creating follow-up ticket to evaluate long-term mitigation (adaptive shaping, per-integration backpressure).

jess: taking on-call at 1744030500. handoff: all mitigations in place, primary owner for monitoring: will, rollback owner: maria. CS contact: kyla. I'll escalate if anything re-escalates. :white_check_mark:
